name: Regex Tester
description: Test regular expressions live: highlight matches, inspect groups and preview replacements, with lookaround and backreferences, and detect catastrophic backtracking risks
help: Matching runs in the local Rust engine (fancy-regex) with lookahead / lookbehind, backreferences and named groups (?P<name>…).
Flags: i ignore case, m multi-line (^ $ per line), s dot matches newline, x ignore whitespace and # comments.
Click a match on the right to locate it; replacements support $0, $1 and ${name}.
Runaway backtracking is stopped automatically so the app never hangs.

Performance tab: statically scans for ReDoS patterns such as nested quantifiers, overlapping alternation and adjacent overlapping quantifiers with rewrite tips, then measures the sample text and auto-generated attack inputs with a step-counting backtracking simulator (behaving like JavaScript, Java or PCRE engines, with step and time limits) to tell linear, polynomial or exponential growth. Everything runs offline.

perf.title: Performance
perf.engineLinear: This tool runs the pattern on a linear-time engine, so it cannot hang here; backtracking engines such as JavaScript, Java, Python and PCRE can, and the risks below apply to them.
perf.engineBacktracking: The pattern uses backreferences or lookaround, so this tool also has to backtrack (with a limit); the risks below apply here too.
perf.noFindings: No known backtracking risk patterns found.

nested_quantifier.title: Nested quantifier
nested_quantifier.explain: A quantifier inside a quantifier lets the same text be split between the inner and outer loops in exponentially many ways; on failure the engine tries them all.
nested_quantifier.fix: Tip: drop the inner quantifier (e.g. (a+)+ → a+), use an atomic group (?>…) or possessive quantifier, or end each repetition with a separator the inner part cannot match.

overlapping_alternation.title: Overlapping alternation
overlapping_alternation.explain: Repeated branches can match the same characters, so every character can take a different branch and the combinations explode on failure.
overlapping_alternation.fix: Tip: merge the branches into one character class (e.g. (\w|\d)+ → \w+) or make the branches start with mutually exclusive characters.

adjacent_quantifiers.title: Adjacent overlapping quantifiers
adjacent_quantifiers.explain: Two neighbouring quantifiers can match the same characters, so a failing match tries every split point and time grows polynomially.
adjacent_quantifiers.fix: Tip: merge them (e.g. \d+\d+ → \d{2,}) or make them match disjoint character sets.

perf.dynamicHint: Simulates a backtracking engine and counts steps; attack inputs come from the most severe finding, doubling in length.
perf.unsupported: The pattern uses features the simulator does not support (such as conditionals or subroutine calls); the benchmark was skipped.
